title: Contemporary Sesame Broccoli and Bell Pepper Salad
shortDescription: Briefly blanched broccoli and raw bell peppers are cooled, dried, and tossed with a sesame-soy vinaigrette.
culturalContext: This contemporary vegetable salad uses Korean pantry seasonings with broccoli and bell pepper. It is not presented as a traditional named banchan, and its descriptive Korean display name requires review.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Clean bowl for potable ice-water bath

ingredients.preparation: cut evenly and washed under running water

instructions.heading: Wash produce
instructions.action: Wash broccoli and whole bell peppers under cool running water; do not use soap or produce wash.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep produce and clean tools away from raw meat and seafood.

instructions.heading: Prepare ice bath and dressing
instructions.action: Make an ice-water bath with potable water in a clean bowl; separately whisk soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, sesame seeds, and garlic.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Ice bath is cold and dressing is uniform.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a sanitized bowl and potable ice and water.

instructions.heading: Blanch broccoli
instructions.action: Boil broccoli in small batches until bright green and crisp-tender.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Stems are crisp-tender and color is bright.
instructions.safetyNote: Prevent boiling-water and steam burns; do not overcrowd the pot.

instructions.heading: Cool promptly
instructions.action: Transfer broccoli immediately with a clean spider to the potable ice bath, then drain as soon as cold.
instructions.safetyNote: Cool promptly and do not leave cooked vegetables in the temperature danger zone.

instructions.heading: Dry and slice
instructions.action: Dry broccoli thoroughly; seed and thinly slice the washed peppers on a clean board.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Vegetables are dry and evenly cut.
instructions.safetyNote: Use ready-to-eat tools that have not contacted raw foods.

instructions.heading: Toss and chill
instructions.action: Toss vegetables with dressing and refrigerate until service.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep cold and observe the 2-hour limit, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C.

grillSetup: No grill required; use a clean produce area and a stable stovetop for blanching.
targetInternalTemperature: Cool promptly and hold at or below 40°F / 4°C.
visualDonenessCues: Broccoli is bright green and crisp-tender
Broccoli is cold and thoroughly drained
Peppers remain crisp and dressing is lightly applied
foodSafetyNotes: Wash produce under running water without soap or bleach.
Use potable ice and water in a clean ice bath.
Cool blanched broccoli promptly to 40°F / 4°C or below, then drain and dry.
Use clean ready-to-eat tools and hold the finished salad cold.
Discard salad held above 40°F / 4°C beyond 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Verify every packaged-ingredient label and segregate tools for diners with allergies.

substitutions: Cauliflower may replace part of the broccoli after separate blanch-time testing.
Use certified gluten-free tamari only after label verification.
ingredientSourcing: Choose compact broccoli florets without yellowing or slime.
Choose firm bell peppers without soft spots.
makeAhead: Blanch, cool, dry, and refrigerate vegetables up to 1 day ahead; dress within 2 hours of service.
storage: Keep covered at or below 40°F / 4°C and use within 2 days.
reheating: Do not reheat; serve chilled or cool.
leftovers: Discard service leftovers beyond time limits or contaminated by used utensils.
servingSuggestions: Serve chilled with grilled lamb or beef.
Add dressing shortly before service for the crispest texture.

faq.question: Why use potable ice water?
faq.answer: The cooked broccoli contacts the bath directly, so the bowl, water, and ice must all be safe and clean.

faq.question: Can I skip drying?
faq.answer: Drying reduces dilution and helps the dressing coat evenly.
